sources.name: Castro, Curley & Hertzog (2021) category norms, US adults, category 'A flower' (proportion of 246 US adults aged 18-80+ listing each): rose .89, tulip .53, daisy .50, lily .30, sunflower .26, daffodil .22, carnation .22, petunia .15, orchid .14, dandelion .12, pansy .11, violet .11, iris .08, lilac .08, peony .08, gardenia .07, marigold .07, mum .06, geranium .05, hydrangea .05; subgroup-only (>=5% in one age group): baby's breath .06, dahlia .06, poppy .06, aster .05, hyacinth .05

sources.name: Spring Hill Nurseries 50-state + DC survey: flower planted most often, from 20 options; states won: rose 19, sunflower 6, daffodil 4, hydrangea 4, peony 4, lavender 3, marigold 2, pansy 2, tulip/lilac/geranium/daylily/orchid/lily/iris 1 each; gerbera, petunia, gardenia, dahlia, violet 0

sources.name: YDAFT Google Trends analysis of 85 flowers, most-searched flower by state (via Lily's Florist 50-state table): rose 10, marigold 5, hydrangea 4, alstroemeria 3, sunflower 3, daisy/hyacinth/lily/poppy/ranunculus/snapdragon/tulip 2 each, aster/azalea/daffodil/dahlia/geranium/iris/lavender/orchid/peony/waxflower/zinnia 1 each

changes_vs_current: New topic. Raw average-position order across 7 people sources (missing = list length + 5, ties by source count): 1 rose 1.29, 2 sunflower 5.36, 3 tulip 5.57, 4 orchid 9.43, 5 lily 9.57, 6 daisy 9.71, 7 peony 10.86, 8 daffodil 11.86, 9 marigold 13.93, 10 pansy 14.07, 11 iris 14.29, 12 carnation 14.43, 13 hydrangea 14.71, 14 lilac 15.14, 15 violet 15.14, 16 petunia 15.29, 17 geranium 15.43, 18 poppy 15.57, 19 gardenia 16.57, 20 dandelion 17.0, 21 chrysanthemum 17.29, 22 snapdragon 18.43, 23 lavender 19.0, 24 hyacinth 19.29 (next: azalea 19.29 with fewer sources, dahlia 19.43, zinnia 20.14, aster 20.29). Moves: (1) Carnation 12 -> 9 (above marigold, pansy, iris): gut-check item; both free-listing sources put it high (Castro #7, Battig #3) and Tellwut lists it; its low average comes only from Spring Hill (carnation was not one of the 20 options) and search-based state wins. Not being offered is not evidence it ranks lower. Gut-check items left below #12 because a source puts them there: Hydrangea #13 (Castro #20 at 5%, absent from Battig 1969, though Spring Hill #4, YDAFT #3, Instagram #8 and Gardening Chores #5 rate it higher); Lilac #14 (Castro #14, Battig #15, Spring Hill tied #12); Lavender #23 (under 5% in Castro, absent from Battig, YDAFT tied #18, although Gardening Chores has it #1 and Spring Hill #6). Merges: mum + chrysanthemum, jonquil + daffodil.
confidence: medium: the top 8 (rose, sunflower, tulip, orchid, lily, daisy, peony, daffodil) are consistent across sources, and the US free-listing norms (Castro 2021) directly measure what adults name. But no large probability-sample US 'favorite flower' poll exists. Sources mix free listing, planting, search and hashtags, and #9-#24 are separated by small margins (14-19 average), so the order of the middle and tail is soft.
